learning_outcomes.text: Study the movement of systems composed of rigid solids subjected to external loading.
Resolve equations of motion under the small movements hypothesis, including linearization to obtain exact solutions, describing vibrations of linear systems.
Address the eigenvalue problem in Solid Dynamics, the notion of modes, and modal decomposition of a material system's response under the small movements hypothesis.
Integrate equations of motion in the general case, using numerical time integration schemes (explicit and implicit Euler, Runge Kutta, Newmark) for linear differential equation systems.
Understand concepts of explicit and implicit schemes, consistency, stability, and precision.
Implement an iterative scheme at each time step for non-linear differential equation systems with implicit formulation, detailing the resolution algorithm based on rewriting the system incrementally.
Be introduced to difficulties arising when differential equations form a constrained differential system.
Develop tools to model mechanical systems to better size them, avoiding oversizing in terms of material and motorization.
Account for vibrations in mechanical system modeling to design systems with less impact on the environment and humans.
Develop modeling tools to foster innovation by facilitating numerical simulation, thus limiting physical experimentation.

syllabus_topics: Vibrations of single degree of freedom systems
Vibrations of n degrees of freedom systems
Time integration of equations of motion
